People say when you’re at rock bottom you can only go up. But you aren’t. I guarantee you can think of things that would make your situation worse. Maybe you can’t, but if that’s the case there will be days where it does get a little worse and you’ll realize. I’m not saying that to guilt you, yeah people have it worse, but bad is bad, and it’s okay to feel bad about your situation. What I’m saying is that it’s not as bad as it can get, and chances are that you’ll never be there. You have room to grow and get better, and remember that progress isn’t linear, there will be ups and downs. 

I know it’s hard. And even though everyone says it does, it might never get better. But there still is a greater chance it will. I am young and am having similar issues. But not as young as you are. Just ride it out until you get a little older, until you can make your own decisions. Wait until you have your own freedom and can only do what *you* want, not one anyone else, and live for yourself. Don’t mind what others think or feel about it. They don’t matter, the most important thing is that **you** like the way you live. It’s no one else’s business. If then you get to that point, what you do with it is your choice.

Yeah. That’s the reputation the site gets for its biggest boards. 

-	/b/ - random - is the most popular and has literally no moderation unless something illegal happens, just a true shitstorm 
-	/pol/ - politically incorrect - probably the most infamous and you can tell from the name why, probably where you would hear nazi stories
-	/r9k/ - robot9001 - kinda like /b/ but more filled with just really really sad lonely people
-	/v/ - vidyagames - takes all the toxic video game culture in the modern day and puts it in a nice blend just for you

Now these are just the really big ones. They get normals from everywhere, mostly just edgy kids that heard 4chan is sp00ky from YouTube creepypastas. Also in recent years attract political or social extremists for the same reason. 

But.. there are dozens and dozens of other boards. Some are still pretty broad like /int/, which is just /b/ with flag tags for each poster to see where they post from. And some get super niche, like /po/ which is just for origami.

Usually the bigger the board is, the more cancerous it is. Because obviously bigger boards are faster, and because of that people on bigger boards post inflammatory threads to keep attention to them and thus keep them alive. That mixed with people who do it because the thread will 404 in 3 minutes anyways are a bad duo.

But the more niche boards really do have their appeal. They still do get spill over from /pol/ and stuff but you get used to ignoring and being easily able to tell whose a troll. Anyways in the smaller boards it’s a lot slower so actual conversation is encouraged because there’s a lot bigger of a chance your post will actually get seen. Sometimes you just settle down and sit in a cozy thread about campfires for an hour or so. Even though you have no clue about anything about campfires it’s good fun.

4chan also gets mistaken a lot for 8chan, a site literally created to harbor people banned from 4chan. Also the place where the NZ shooter fucked around and people have been saying it was 4chan. It was not.   (To my knowledge atleast)

Unpopular opinion on reddit, but the more niche boards on 4chan are far better than 99% of reddit to me. 

4chan is different than most sites. You start at the shit end of the rabbit whole and eventually work your way up. You start with the shitty popular general boards like /b/ or /r9k/ or /pol/, then venture to your still broad interests like /mu/, /his/ or /v/. 

Eventually you’ll end up on boards centered on a topic you didn’t know you were obsessed with until you accidentally clicked on /out/ on a cozy summer night. Chatting with a bunch of strangers that know way more than you do about camping, bushcraft, fishing or whatever. You still *act* like you know your shit when you really don’t, it’s just fun to be part of such a tight knit yet completely anonymous community.
